before:
Kaltenbacher's 2024 paper treats the three-dimensional unit ball with background conductivity $\sigma_{\rm bg}\equiv1$, quadratic penalty $\check R(\sigma)=\frac12\|\sigma\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}^2$, $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, and truth $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. Its Theorem 10 reports a logarithmic VSC exponent

$$\nu_{\rm paper}:=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_1-1},$$

with $b=3/4$, and Corollary 11 reports a conductivity-norm rate using that exponent divided by the source parameter $\widetilde p$ for the joint, split, and frozen-Newton methods. These printed formulas are source assertions; the locally proved EIT conclusions use the corrected exponent and parameter qualifications below.

The cited Weidling Theorem 6.15 at $p=2$ gives denominator $s_2-1$ in the corresponding logarithmic exponent. In addition, the quadratic Bregman distance is one half the squared $H^{s_1}$ norm error, so a Bregman rate with logarithmic exponent $\nu$ yields a norm exponent $\nu/2$; this abstract implication alone does not supply every exponent reported by Corollary 11. The sufficient parameter coupling in the abstract rate theorem requires $\alpha H(c/\alpha)\asymp\delta^2$ for a fixed $c>0$. For a logarithmic index with $H(q)\asymp(\log q)^{-\nu}$, no pure-power choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^{\widetilde p}$ with $0<\widetilde p\le2$ satisfies this two-sided coupling. Kaltenbacher's Remark 1 separately asserts that pure powers still give the same logarithmic rate; that separate assertion needs an independent derivation and is not ruled out solely by failure of the sufficient coupling. The local joint and frozen EIT theorems assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, use the corrected exponent $\nu=(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)/(s_2-1)$, retain the entire stated Sobolev/Besov truth range, and prove the conductivity norm exponent $\nu/2$. They give balanced parameters, every strict pure power $0<\widetilde p<2$, and the nominal endpoint $\widetilde p=2$ with an explicit stronger actual-noise condition. The universal abstract endpoint assertion under arbitrary deterministic noise bounded only by $\delta$ is false, as shown by the exact quadratic counterexample in the endpoint lemma; that example does not claim to be an EIT-specific counterexample.

The local application uses mean-zero Neumann currents and boundary-mean-zero Neumann states. Its data space is the centered sequence $(\mathscr N_\sigma-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k}$ in $\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$, or equivalently the corresponding affine translate for absolute voltages. This centering is necessary: at the background conductivity $1$, the uncentered voltage columns have norms $1/\ell$ with multiplicity $2\ell+1$, so their squared sum diverges. The centered Neumann-map differentiability, sharp $H^1$ logarithmic stability, exact intrinsic Sobolev/Besov source inequality, augmented factorization and inverse, frozen Taylor estimate, and regularizer/penalty compatibility now have local proofs. The sharp stability proof retains the Fourier modulation in the CGO remainder and integrates its negative-Sobolev norm before absorption; it does not use the invalid unmodulated pointwise inference in the printed Weidling proof.
